name: Bustarviejo penal labour camp
story: After the war the regime used political prisoners as forced labour on public works under the 'redemption of sentences through work' scheme. At Bustarviejo, prisoners built the Madrid–Burgos railway between 1944 and 1952, living in a camp that has been studied by archaeologists of the CSIC and the Comunidad de Madrid. It is one of the few such camps in Spain whose remains can be seen, and complements Cuelgamuros as evidence of prison labour.
see: Foundations of three compounds, guard posts, a punishment cell and nearby railway cuttings and tunnels.
plan: Signposted path outside the village; free, open access. Allow an hour.
